subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Test count decreased: the old 'contentstack live preview' describe block had 5 tests; the new 'live preview' block has only 3. Two setHost fallback tests were dropped: (1) 'should call setHost with CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is unset' and (2) 'should not call setHost when neither CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST nor CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST is set'. Review criterion (2) requires the total test count not decrease. These dropped tests covered important fallback behavior that is now unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-add the two missing tests: one verifying setHost falls back to CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is unset, and one verifying setHost is not called when neither host env var is set.

issues.description: contentstack.Stack(options as any) widens the `any` cast to the entire options object without an explanatory comment. The original code used a narrower `as unknown as contentstack.LivePreview` cast only on the live_preview property. Casting the whole options object to `any` suppresses all type checking on api_key, delivery_token, environment, branch, and fetchOptions — a TypeScript strict compliance regression.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the `as any` from the Stack constructor call. Instead, type the live_preview property correctly. If the contentstack SDK types don't include preview_token on LivePreview, use a narrow cast only on that property (e.g. `live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN } as unknown as contentstack.LivePreview`) with an explanatory comment, or extend the SDK type declaration.

issues.description: (query as any).addParam("live_preview", "true") and (query as any).addParam("preview_hash", ...) use untyped `any` without an explanatory comment. While the file has a top-level eslint-disable for no-explicit-any, review criteria require an explanatory comment for each `any` usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an inline comment explaining why the cast is necessary (e.g. `// Contentstack SDK query type doesn't expose addParam in its TypeScript definitions`), or cast to a narrower interface that includes addParam.

issues.description: The `enable` field in ICommonContentstackConfig.live_preview is dead code — it is never read in setCommonConfig. The code hardcodes addParam("live_preview", "true") unconditionally whenever any live_preview object is present, rather than gating on live_preview.enable. This means a caller passing { enable: false, preview_hash: 'x' } would still get live_preview=true added to the query.
issues.suggestedFix: Gate the addParam call on enable: `if (live_preview?.enable) { (query as any).addParam("live_preview", "true"); ... }`. Alternatively, remove `enable` from the interface if it is not intended to be forwarded.

issues.description: The new code replaces the SDK's livePreviewQuery method with raw addParam calls, hand-rolling query parameter logic that the Contentstack SDK provides natively. While the old livePreviewQuery call was also broken (it referenced live_preview.live_preview which no longer exists in the interface, and query.content_type_uid which is not a standard query property), the correct fix is to use livePreviewQuery with the updated interface shape, not to bypass the SDK entirely with low-level addParam calls.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the SDK's livePreviewQuery method with the correct parameters from the updated interface, e.g. `if (live_preview?.preview_hash) { (query as any).livePreviewQuery({ live_preview: live_preview.preview_hash, content_type_uid: contentTypeUid }); }`. If addParam is intentionally the correct approach for this SDK version, add a comment explaining why livePreviewQuery is not used.
